Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Transient stimulus with delayed ATAC/CUT&Tag readout
ideas.description: Expose cells to a brief stimulus (e.g., TPA or inflammatory cue) and then profile chromatin accessibility and AP-1 (FOS/JUN) binding by ATAC-seq and CUT&Tag after a long washout. Persistent accessibility at AP-1 motif sites after the signal and AP-1 activity have returned to baseline would indicate a memory-like chromatin state. Like the material's string of short, mostly non-repeating tokens, this relies on individually unique 'marks' being retained after the signal ends.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 degradation during the memory phase
ideas.description: Use a dTAG/auxin degron on JUN/FOS, or a dominant-negative such as A-FOS, at defined times: during the priming stimulus, or only during the washout. Then test whether the primed enhanced re-response is lost. Loss when AP-1 is removed only during the washout shows ongoing AP-1 is needed to maintain memory; loss only when removed during priming shows it acts as an initiator.

ideas.title: Single-cell live imaging of AP-1 reporter history
ideas.description: Image AP-1 activity with a live reporter or a FOS/JUN biosensor across repeated stimulation pulses in single cells, then relate each cell's prior pulse history to its later response amplitude. Cell-to-cell heterogeneity and the persistence of individual cells' response states over days and divisions would distinguish true memory from continued signaling.

ideas.title: Synthetic AP-1 site perturbation at memory enhancers
ideas.description: Use CRISPR to mutate AP-1 motifs or tether dCas9-KRAB or dCas9-p300 at specific primed enhancers, and measure re-stimulation transcription (RNA-seq/PRO-seq) and H3K27ac. If memory-linked genes lose faster or stronger secondary responses only when their AP-1 motifs are disrupted, this shows AP-1 binding is causal rather than merely correlated.

ideas.title: Mitotic bookmarking and inheritance assay
ideas.description: Synchronize and sort primed cells, and map FOS/JUN occupancy on mitotic chromosomes by CUT&RUN. Follow lineage-tracked daughter cells through several divisions, measuring whether enhanced responsiveness and AP-1-associated accessibility are inherited. Retained AP-1 binding on mitotic chromatin and transmission of primed responses to daughter cells would support heritable memory.
